Is there any design doc for the same

I feel it is existing design
PCIeDevices routes, PCIeSlots routes also behave the same. 
When  the devices are not populated the collection shows empty. 

example for TPM case:
```
{
    "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Chassis/<Chassis-id>/TrustedComponents",
    "@odata.type": "#TrustedComponentCollection.TrustedComponentCollection",
    "Members": [],
    "Members@odata.count": 0,
    "Name": "Trusted Component Collection"
}
```
Done
Is TPM enabled by default for all the platforms?
Yes, If there's no TPM device the TPM collection will be empty.

So there's an equivalent patch to https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr ?

Please link it.

yes there is a code merged in smbios-mdr 
https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr/commit/5af42bbf374907888c09d7aaf2cbf74d74c7707d
Can you talk about the association this uses? Talk about the PDI ?
There is an association that links the chassis (representing the system's physical enclosure) to trusted components. This helps in other components to access the TPM information.

I haven't looked at the DMTF specs.


But I don't see how a tpm can protect physical components like a chassis. it's not generally connected to tamper switches.

I would think it should be associated to (in redfish terminology linked to a list of) logical objects that are being validated extending the PCRs.   this includes computer system and manager but could also be storage controller, network controller, accelerator, or anything similar through spdm.

TPM are contained in chassis. This is similar to other implementations in smbios-mdr. 
Example:
CPU https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr/blob/master/src/cpu.cpp#L261
DIMM https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr/blob/master/src/dimm.cpp#L114
PCIe Slot https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr/blob/master/src/pcieslot.cpp#L65
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/smbios-mdr/+/79995 removed associations
Doesn't the redfish service validator also need to walk this schema?

TrustedComponents are under Chassis (/redfish/v1/Chassis/<Chassis-ID>/TrustedComponents)
So in the commit I meant redfish validator test passed for /redfish/v1/Chassis/<chassis-id>

Just make sure the Validator walked the link to TrustedComponents. Your wording here makes it sound like you have other redfish validator errors, but /redfish/v1/Chassis/<chassis-id> is good. That isn't enough, please make sure TrustedComponents, doesn't have validator errors / you have not introduced any new validator errors

I think we can change this method to getTrustedComponentPaths, so that we can extend this to TPM and SPDM.
The reason I kept this as `getTPMPaths` is because after getting TPM paths we could add method to get SPDMPaths
I agree that this method can be generic to handle TPM or SPDM-capable devices
Resolved.

SPDM design(https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/redfish-spdm-attestation.md) uses /TrustedComponents in D-Bus object path itself. Where as smbios-mdr uses trusted components association(https://github.com/openbmc/smbios-mdr/blob/master/src/tpm.cpp#L50).

Can we rely on tpm interface with base chassis path directly here?. With that when we add TrustedComponent interface path for SPDM objects we can extend this method.

Or we need to come up with common path or association for TPM and SPDM.

SMBIOS-MDR currently doesn't implement direct path.
in smbios-mdr we have common inventory object and association is used to fetch the objects.

I am thinking if we keep /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory as path and do a SubTree look up on path which implements TPM interface(now), TrustedComponent interface(later) we can easily re-use this function instead of adding trusted_components to the path.
Done

So, I dont have the ways to test the implementation.

This seems to be only consider the fact that a TPM is only for host/bios.

TPM's can also be connected to BMC, so we would probably also need to have TrustedComponents on `v1/Managers/{}/`

And then based on which object Inventory.Item.Tpm object is associated to we would have to implement the route for it (it can be a chassis or even a BMC). If this is something that is being planned for another patch, atleast we should make sure this patch does not have any assumptions.

Okay, the system which I use doesn't have TPM connected to BMC. So, I was not aware of this use-case. Thanks a lot for this info.

I can help you with the testing if needed.

`trusted_componets` association itself is not documented in the phosphor-dbus-interface. I am not sure why smbios-mdr did not mandate it.

But the association needs to be documented first in PDI, before it gets used in anywhere else.

We do have similar case for cpu and dimm in smbios-mdr. As per https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/TrustedComponent.interface.yaml we have reported_by and protecting association. Do we recommend we add the same to https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/Tpm.interface.yaml ?

If `TrustedComponent.Interface.yaml` already documented the association, why did we add a new association `trusted_components` in smbios_mdr ? 

seems like `protecting` would be the one to use ? and i dont think we need to add a new association to the Tpm.Interface.yaml if we are using the TrustedComponent.Interface ?
Okay, the Interface used in smbios-mdr is `TPM.Interface` and NOT `TrustedComponent.Interface`. So, should we be using TrustedComponent.Interface in smbios-mdr ? instead of TPM ?
This association needs to be documented in PDI
Have raised MR to remove the association https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/smbios-mdr/+/79995. Will move this MR to WIP and once the smbios-mdr MR is merged will work on this
are we sure that all SPDM capable devices are Discrete type?

This should ideally come from `TrustedComponentType` dbus property from who ever implements https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/TrustedComponent.interface.yaml#L5 and not hardcoded.
All TPM components are Discrete. Will have PDI for Item.TPM for TrustedComponentType

The TPM interface I used was https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/Tpm.interface.yaml
There is no property for indicating `TrustedComponentType`. Do you recommend adding it ?
Done
Not a redfish expert, but I thought TrsutedComponent dbus interface is added by keeping TrustedComponents redfish schema in mind, so we should be using that instead (IMO)
The reason TPM.Interface was used is the SMBIOS type 43 record defines TPM information. So thought TPM.Interface was the right one to be used

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/smbios-mdr/+/79995
As suggested used `TrustedComponent.interface`

we typically don't check for empty here. Is there a reason you do? 
Why not add the other properties from the interface?
When we get TPM information from SMBIOS records currently there is no way to get serial number, uuid, etc. Hence, taking care of empty strings here
